places.name: Rock Garden of Chandigarh
places.description: A 40-acre visionary sculpture garden created secretly by Nek Chand over 18 years using industrial and household waste, broken ceramic chinaware, and recycled glass bracelets.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: One of the most extraordinary folk art environments on earth. Walking through its narrow gorge passages and mosaic plazas reveals Chandigarh’s soul beyond modernist grid lines.
places.bestTimeToVisit: Morning (09:00 – 11:30 AM) or late afternoon to avoid midday sun.

places.name: Sukhna Lake & Bird Sanctuary Trail
places.description: A pristine 3 km² rain-fed lake at the foothills of the Shivalik range created in 1958 by damming the Sukhna Choe. Features a scenic walking promenade, solar boat rides, and the quiet Garden of Silence at the far end.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: The defining open-air ritual of Chandigarh. Watching the sunset turn the Shivalik foothills purple from the walking track is an unmissable local experience.

places.name: Sector 17 City Plaza
places.description: Designed by Le Corbusier as the pedestrian civic heart of the city. Broad concrete boulevards lined with trees, musical fountains, historic government book depots, and local retail stores.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: Experience Le Corbusier’s modernist pedestrian architecture without traffic. Great for soft-serve ice cream, evening fountain shows, and vintage bookstore browsing.

places.name: Pal Dhaba Sector 28
places.address: Booth No. 165 & 166, Inner Market, Sector 28-D, Chandigarh
places.description: An iconic Punjabi culinary institution serving authentic robust dishes since 1960. Renowned for its slow-cooked Butter Chicken, Rogan Josh, Dal Makhani, and tandoori garlic naans.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: Universally hailed by generations of Chandigarh residents and visiting dignitaries. Unpretentious, loud, energetic, and delivers legendary Punjabi comfort food.
places.bestTimeToVisit: Dinner (08:00 – 10:00 PM) or lunch around 01:30 PM

places.name: Capitol Complex & Open Hand Monument
places.description: The monumental UNESCO World Heritage centerpiece designed by Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier. Comprises the High Court, Secretariat, Legislative Assembly, and the 26-meter rotating Open Hand monument symbolizing "open to give, open to receive".
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: A landmark of 20th-century global architecture. Its brutalist concrete forms, ramp geometries, and raw symbolism cannot be found anywhere else in Asia.

places.name: Virgin Courtyard
places.description: An enchanting sunlit Italian restaurant with white Mediterranean stone arches, cobblestone courtyard seating under bougainvillea, and hand-rolled pasta paired with sangria.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: Chandigarh’s crown jewel for romantic dining and peaceful afternoon coffees. The serene courtyard ambiance feels transportive.
places.bestTimeToVisit: Evening for candlelit dinner (08:00 PM) or late lunch (02:00 PM)

places.name: Sector 8 Artisan Coffee & Bakeries
places.description: The creative epicenter of Chandigarh’s contemporary café culture. Features specialty pour-overs, sourdough bakeries, artisanal gelato, and indie boutique studios.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: Where local entrepreneurs and creatives spend their mornings with freshly roasted single-origin brews. Perfect starting base for a Chandigarh day.
places.bestTimeToVisit: Morning breakfast (09:00 – 11:00 AM) or coffee break (04:00 PM)

places.name: Qila Mubarak Royal Complex
places.description: Founded in 1763 by Baba Ala Singh, the 10-acre fort complex is a rare synthesis of Mughal and Rajasthani architecture. Houses the majestic Ran Baas guest palace and Darbar Hall with Belgian cut-glass chandeliers and Maharaja armor collections.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: The epicenter of Patiala Shahi royal history. Stepping into the ancient courtyards reveals the immense grandeur of Punjab’s princely state heritage.

places.name: Sheesh Mahal & Medal Gallery
places.description: The Palace of Mirrors constructed under Maharaja Narinder Singh in 1847. Surrounded by a scenic moat with a Lakshman Jhula style rope bridge, housing Kangra miniature frescoes and the world’s largest collection of royal orders and decorations.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: The suspension bridge over the water body in front of the mirrored palace creates one of the most picturesque sunset frames in all of Punjab.

places.name: Baradari Royal Gardens & Pavilion
places.address: Near Baradari Palace, Circuit House Road, Patiala
places.description: A sprawling 19th-century royal Mughal garden with 12 open gates (Baradari) commissioned by Maharaja Rajinder Singh. Dotted with ancient banyan trees, rare botanical imports, and colonial marble fountains.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: A tranquil oasis where Patiala locals gather for early morning walking and quiet conversations amidst century-old royal trees.

places.name: Adalat Bazaar & Phulkari Hub
places.description: The ancient bustling commercial heart of Patiala. Renowned worldwide for authentic artisan Phulkari embroidery, traditional handcrafted Patiala Shahi juttis, and authentic Parandis directly from master weavers.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: No trip to Patiala is complete without feeling the heavy silk floss needlework of genuine Phulkari. Authentic heritage craftsmanship at direct artisan rates.

places.name: Patiala Shahi Lassi & Gopal Sweets
places.address: Near Phul Cinema & Adalat Bazaar, Patiala
places.description: Legendary brass-churned Patiala Shahi lassi served in deep terracotta kulhads with a thick layer of fresh malai, paired with piping hot kachoris and rich dry fruit pinnis.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: The undisputed taste of authentic Patiala. A single glass of this velvety saffron-topped lassi is a royal meal in itself.

places.name: Gurdwara Dukh Niwaran Sahib
places.description: Sacred Sikh shrine commemorating the visit of the ninth Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib. Pilgrims revere the sacred sarovar, known for spiritual solace and healing traditions.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: The peaceful kirtan echoing across the illuminated marble sarovar at dawn or dusk delivers profound spiritual grounding.
places.bestTimeToVisit: Early morning Amrit Vela (05:00 AM) or evening sunset kirtan

places.name: Kasturba Sewa Mandir & Organic Orchard
places.address: Kasturba Dham, Near Old GT Road, Rajpura, 140401
places.description: Established in 1947–1950 during the post-partition resettlement under Gandhian constructive workers. Still preserves traditional handloom khadi spinning, organic amla orchards, and historical archives of Punjab’s refugee rehabilitation story.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: The emotional and historical cornerstone of modern Rajpura. You can purchase genuine organic honey, khadi fabrics, and learn an inspiring tale of community rebuilding.

places.name: Eagle & Heritage GT Road Dhabas
places.address: NH 44 (Old GT Road Junction), Rajpura By-Pass, 140401
places.description: Legendary Grand Trunk Road highway dhabas that have served cross-country truckers and food connoisseurs for over 50 years. Famous for clay-oven tandoori chicken, sarson ka saag with makki roti, and rich dal tadka.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: The definitive highway culinary stopover between Chandigarh and Delhi. Charred tandoori rotis dripping with home-churned white butter.
places.bestTimeToVisit: Late dinner (08:30 – 11:30 PM) or breakfast chai with stuffed paranthas

places.name: Rajpura Historic Grain & Spice Mandi
places.description: One of Malwa Punjab’s key agricultural hubs. Features traditional wholesale spice traders, seasonal jaggery (gur) makers, and bustling morning auctions of golden wheat and basmati rice.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: An immersive sensory window into Punjab’s agrarian heartland. Photographers will love the golden morning dust, burlap sacks, and cup of kadak adrak chai.

places.name: Gurdwara Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib
places.description: A serene historic gurdwara marking the path traveled by the ninth Sikh Guru toward Delhi. Revered for its peaceful sanctum, shaded banyan trees, and community langar.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: A quiet, unhurried spiritual haven away from highway hustle. Enjoy community langar served with warmth and humility.

places.name: Neelam Sweets & Traditional Kachori Hub
places.address: Near Focal Point & Station Road, Rajpura
places.description: Renowned for morning crispy dal kachoris served with spicy aloo sabzi, freshly prepared hot jalebis, and seasonal pinni sweets prepared with pure desi ghee.
places.whyPlanRupeeRecommends: The most popular breakfast stop for residents and commuters passing through Rajpura junction. Unrivaled freshly fried kachoris.

place_reviews.comment: Unbelievable creativity. The transition from tiny stone alleyways into massive amphitheatres made of recycled porcelain is mesmerizing. Visited as part of my Day 1 PlanRupee roadmap.
The walking path during early morning is calm and therapeutic. Local guide Simran told us to walk all the way to the silence zone instead of staying near the crowded ticket counter.
Butter Chicken lives up to its 60-year fame. Creamy without being cloying, deep charred smokiness from the tandoor. You must order with garlic naan.
The Ran Baas courtyards and Darbar Hall armory are a treasure trove. Gurpreet was our local advisor through PlanRupee and explained the Sikh-Mughal architectural synergy with immense depth.
Thickest lassi I have had in India. Served in a heavy clay kulhad with a spoon because the malai layer is literally an inch thick! Absolutely essential Patiala stop.
A quiet, inspiring historical oasis. The amla products and handspun khadi shawls are genuine and support rural women weavers.
Proper midnight highway dhaba flavor. Dal makhani simmered on coal fires and crispy tandoori rotis with homemade white butter.

local_reviews.comment: Simran completely transformed our weekend in Chandigarh. Instead of doing the standard tourist bus routine, she curated three private courtyard cafes and an evening date table at Virgin Courtyard that blew us away.
Super fast replies on WhatsApp! She recommended Pal Dhaba Sector 28 and guided me exactly what to order. Worth every rupee of the consultation fee.

Gurpreet’s knowledge of Patiala royal history is unmatched. He arranged direct access to an authentic Phulkari master artisan in Adalat Bazaar where we bought family heirlooms without tourist markups.
Harleen helped me plan an architectural photography tour between Chandigarh Capitol Complex and Rajpura’s post-partition sites. Exceptional insights on Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret.
Amanjit knows every dhaba cook between Rajpura and Patiala. He picked the exact spot for fresh sarson ka saag and early morning grain mandi auctions. Authentic rustic Punjab.
